parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured clay WOMAN (female, not the man in the reference: copy only the reference's clay style, pose and framing) with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin, a thin neck and narrow hunched shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Pink flesh-toned clay skin, a long black wimple veil covering her hair. A cracked grey clay face with deep empty black eye sockets and a crudely stitched-shut mouth. Wearing a tattered black habit with a stained white collar and a rusty chain rosary, her right fist grips a rusty serrated bone saw, a giant red-and-cream striped circus mallet slung behind her back. A slate-grey pressed-clay backdrop. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, her body is in three-quarter view and her head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Her right hand grips the held weapon in a tight clenched fist seen from the back of the hand, knuckles toward the camera, palm hidden, the blade angled up and out; her other hand hangs open. EYES: the cracked grey face covers the whole face; both eyes are deep empty black hollow sockets with nothing inside; no eyeballs, no pink skin face, no fleshy eyes beside, behind or above the grey face. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
